German says “ich tat dasselbe”. In English the must not be missing: the same.

traps.bad: The costs of the new plan are lower than the old plan.
traps.good: The costs of the new plan are lower than those of the old plan.
why: Verglichen werden Kosten mit Kosten, nicht Kosten mit einem Plan. Das Deutsche sagt „als die des alten Plans“, im Englischen braucht man those of.
Costs are compared with costs, not costs with a plan. German says “als die des alten Plans”, English needs those of.

traps.bad: Can you join us? Yes, I would like.
traps.good: Can you join us? Yes, I would like to.
why: Im Deutschen antwortet man „Ich würde gern“ ohne Infinitiv. Im Englischen bleibt to als Platzhalter für den weggelassenen Infinitiv stehen: I would like to.
In German the answer is just “Ich würde gern”, without an infinitive. In English to stays as a stand-in for the dropped infinitive: I would like to.

core: Du baust Information um ein Nomen herum: ohne that („the system we tested“), mit Partizip („the files stored in the cloud“), mit ’s oder of und mit to + Grundform („the best way to reduce costs“).

You build information around a noun: without that (“the system we tested”), with a participle (“the files stored in the cloud”), with ’s or of and with to + base form (“the best way to reduce costs”).
why: Gute Texte auf C1 packen viel Information in wenige Wörter. Statt zweier Sätze steht eine Nominalgruppe. Wann ja, wann nein: In Berichten und Mails spart das Platz. Im Gespräch klingen mehr als zwei Zusätze vor oder hinter einem Nomen schwer, dann lieber zwei Sätze.

Good C1 writing packs a lot of information into few words. Instead of two sentences there is one noun phrase. When yes, when no: in reports and emails this saves space. In conversation more than two additions around a noun sound heavy, so use two sentences.
contrast: Nicht verwechseln: -ing hat das Nomen aktiv getan (the team working), die 3. Form passiv (the files stored). Ein that darf nur fehlen, wenn es Objekt ist, nie als Subjekt.

Do not mix up: -ing means the noun is doing it (the team working), the past participle means it undergoes it (the files stored). A that may only be dropped when it is the object, never as the subject.
steps: Welche Information gehört zum Nomen? Packe sie direkt dahinter.
Satz ohne that: nur wenn das Pronomen Objekt ist.
Partizip: -ing aktiv, 3. Form passiv.
Nach first, last, only, way: to + Grundform.
Which information belongs to the noun? Put it right after it.
Clause without that: only when the pronoun is the object.
Participle: -ing active, past participle passive.
After first, last, only, way: to + base form.
forms: the + superlative / first / only + noun + (that) + subject + verb
This is the most reliable system we have tested.
The team working on the migration meets every Monday.
Person / company + 's + noun · noun + of + thing
The company's new CEO starts on Monday.
the first / last / only / best way + to + base form
She was the first customer to sign the new contract.
noun + participle + phrase · the extent to which … · those who …
We offer a solution tailored to your needs.
signals: the team working / the files stored
the first to / the only one to
tailored to / the extent to which

traps.bad: This is the most reliable system what we have tested.
traps.good: This is the most reliable system we have tested.
why: Das Deutsche sagt „das System, das wir getestet haben“ mit Relativpronomen. Im Englischen entfällt es oft ganz, und „what“ ist nach einem Nomen nie ein Relativpronomen.
German says “das System, das wir getestet haben” with a relative pronoun. English often drops it, and “what” is never a relative pronoun after a noun.

traps.bad: The people involving in the project agreed.
traps.good: The people involved in the project agreed.
why: Die Beteiligten werden beteiligt, sie beteiligen nichts. Passive Bedeutung braucht die 3. Form, nicht -ing.
The people are involved by others, they do not involve anything. Passive meaning needs the past participle, not -ing.

traps.bad: The meeting from yesterday was canceled.
traps.good: Yesterday's meeting was canceled.
why: Bei Zeitangaben steht ’s: yesterday’s meeting. Das deutsche „das Meeting von gestern“ führt zu „from yesterday“.
With time words ’s is used: yesterday’s meeting. The German “das Meeting von gestern” leads to “from yesterday”.

traps.bad: This is the best way for reduce costs.
traps.good: This is the best way to reduce costs.
why: Das Deutsche sagt „der beste Weg, um … zu“. Im Englischen folgt nach way direkt to + Grundform, nicht for.
German says “der beste Weg, um … zu”. In English to + base form follows way directly, not for.

core: Wahrscheinlichkeit hat Stufen: may well (durchaus möglich), is likely to (wahrscheinlich), is bound to (so gut wie sicher). Dazu kommt der Nominalstil: There is a good chance that …
Probability comes in steps: may well (quite possible), is likely to (probable), is bound to (almost certain). The noun style adds: There is a good chance that …
why: Im Berufsalltag sagst du nicht nur „vielleicht“. Wer Stufen kennt, schätzt klar ein und bleibt trotzdem vorsichtig. Wann ja, wann nein: Prognosen und Risikoberichte brauchen die Stufen, im lockeren Gespräch genügt oft „probably“.

At work you say more than “maybe”. If you know the steps you can judge clearly and still stay careful. When yes, when no: forecasts and risk reports need the steps, in casual talk “probably” is often enough.
contrast: Nicht verwechseln: may well ist stärker als may, aber schwächer als bound to. Nach bound und likely steht to + Grundform, nach chance ein that-Satz oder of.
Do not mix up: may well is stronger than may but weaker than bound to. After bound and likely comes to + base form, after chance a that-clause or of.
steps: Wie sicher bist du? Wähle die Stufe.
Durchaus möglich: may/might/could well + Grundform.
Wahrscheinlich oder fast sicher: likely to, bound to + Grundform.
Sachlich: there is a good chance that …
How sure are you? Choose the step.
Quite possible: may/might/could well + base form.
Probable or almost certain: likely to, bound to + base form.
Factual: there is a good chance that …
forms: may / might / could + well + base form
The client may well reject the first offer.
be bound to, be sure to
be bound to, be sure to
be bound / sure / certain + to + base form
Prices are bound to rise after the merger.
be likely to, be unlikely to
be likely to, be unlikely to
be (un)likely + to + base form · It is likely that …
The update is likely to be ready on Friday.
There is a (good) chance that … · It is (highly) probable that …
There is a good chance that the supplier will agree.
signals: is bound to / are bound to
be bound to, be sure to
be bound to, be sure to
is likely to / is unlikely to
be likely to, be unlikely to
be likely to, be unlikely to
a good chance / a slim chance

traps.bad: The client may be well reject the first offer.
traps.good: The client may well reject the first offer.
why: Das deutsche „durchaus“ steht frei im Satz. Im Englischen steht well fest direkt hinter may, might oder could, ohne be dazwischen.
The German “durchaus” can stand almost anywhere. In English well stands right after may, might or could, with no be between them.

traps.bad: Prices are bound rising after the merger.
traps.good: Prices are bound to rise after the merger.
why: Nach bound steht to und die Grundform. Das -ing kommt von Wendungen wie „look forward to“ und passt hier nicht.
After bound comes to and the base form. The -ing comes from phrases like “look forward to” and does not fit here.

traps.bad: The update is likely that it is ready on Friday.
traps.good: The update is likely to be ready on Friday.
why: Nach dem Subjekt steht likely + to + Grundform. „It is likely that …“ geht auch, aber dann beginnt der Satz mit it.
After the subject comes likely + to + base form. “It is likely that …” works too, but then the sentence starts with it.

traps.bad: It exists a good chance that the supplier will agree.
traps.good: There is a good chance that the supplier will agree.
why: Das deutsche „es besteht“ führt zu „it exists“. Englisch sagt there is.
German “es besteht” leads to “it exists”. English says there is.

core: Die Verlaufsform zeigt, dass etwas läuft, vorläufig ist oder höflich klingen soll. Zustände (know, need, belong) bleiben meist in der einfachen Form. Ausnahmen: think (nachdenken), have (essen), see (treffen).

The continuous shows that something is under way, temporary, or meant to sound polite. States (know, need, belong) mostly stay in the simple form. Exceptions: think (consider), have (eat), see (meet).
why: Im Beruf beschreibst du Trends („We are seeing …“) und bittest weich („I was wondering if …“). Wann ja, wann nein: Die weiche Bitte passt bei Fremden und Vorgesetzten, unter Kollegen wirkt „Can you …?“ normal. Zustandsverben bleiben immer einfach.

At work you describe trends (“We are seeing …”) and ask softly (“I was wondering if …”). When yes, when no: the soft request fits strangers and superiors, among colleagues “Can you …?” sounds normal. Stative verbs always stay simple.
contrast: Nicht verwechseln: Im Deutschen gibt es keine Verlaufsform. Aus „ich kenne“ wird nie „I am knowing“. Aus „er ist müde“ wird nie „he is being tired“.
Do not mix up: German has no continuous. “Ich kenne” never becomes “I am knowing”. “Er ist müde” never becomes “he is being tired”.
steps: Zustand, Meinung oder Besitz? Einfache Form.
Läuft die Veränderung gerade? are seeing, is getting.
Weiche Bitte? was hoping, was wondering + if you could.
Verhalten für kurze Zeit? is being + Adjektiv.
State, opinion or possession? Simple form.
Is a change under way? are seeing, is getting.
Soft request? was hoping, was wondering + if you could.
Behavior for a short time? is being + adjective.
forms: be + -ing with seeing, finding, getting, becoming, growing
We are seeing a clear rise in demand.
I was hoping / wondering / thinking + (that / if) + you could …
I was hoping you could review the draft.
be being + behavior adjective · always + -ing for annoyance
You are being unreasonable about the deadline.
Stative verb in the simple form: know, believe, understand, need, want, belong, own
We need a decision by Friday.
signals: i was hoping / i am hoping

traps.bad: Prices rise at the moment because of the new tax.
traps.good: Prices are rising at the moment because of the new tax.
why: Mit „at the moment“ oder „currently“ läuft der Vorgang gerade. Dafür braucht das Englische die Verlaufsform, die einfache Form passt nicht.
With “at the moment” or “currently” the process is under way right now. English needs the continuous for that, the simple form does not fit.

traps.bad: I was wondering could you send me the file.
traps.good: I was wondering if you could send me the file.
why: Nach wondering folgt ein Nebensatz mit if und normaler Satzstellung. Eine Frage mit vorgezogenem could passt hier nicht.
After wondering a clause with if and normal word order follows. A question with could in front does not fit here.

traps.bad: She is being tired after the long flight.
traps.good: She is tired after the long flight.
why: Being steht nur bei Verhalten, das man steuern kann. Müdigkeit ist ein Zustand, deshalb heißt es einfach is tired.
Being is used only for behavior you can control. Tiredness is a state, so it is simply is tired.

traps.bad: I am knowing the answer to your question.
traps.good: I know the answer to your question.
why: Know beschreibt einen Zustand. Zustände stehen in der einfachen Form, nicht mit be + -ing.
Know describes a state. States stay in the simple form, not with be + -ing.

core: Von der Vergangenheit aus gesehen verschieben sich die Zukunftsformen: will wird would, am going to wird was going to. Dazu kommen was about to und was to.
Seen from the past, the future forms shift: will becomes would, am going to becomes was going to. Was about to and was to are added.
why: Im Beruf erzählst du von geplatzten Plänen („We were going to launch …“) und Verläufen („She would later lead …“). Wann ja, wann nein: Im Alltag genügt „was going to“, „was to“ und „would later“ gehören eher in Berichte und Erzählungen.

At work you talk about plans that fell through (“We were going to launch …”) and careers (“She would later lead …”). When yes, when no: in everyday talk “was going to” is enough, “was to” and “would later” fit reports and stories better.
contrast: Nicht verwechseln: Das deutsche „sollte“ ist nicht immer should. Für Vorgesehenes aus der Vergangenheit sagt Englisch was to oder was supposed to.
Do not mix up: the German “sollte” is not always should. For something meant to happen in the past English says was to or was supposed to.
steps: Blickst du aus der Vergangenheit auf Späteres?
Plan von damals: was going to.
Kurz davor: was about to + Grundform.
Später geschah es: would. Vorgesehen: was to.
Do you look from the past at something later?
Plan from back then: was going to.
Just before: was about to + base form.
It happened later: would. Meant to be: was to.
forms: was / were going to + base form
We were going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.
was / were about to + base form (… when …)
I was about to leave when the client called.
She joined the firm in 2015 and would later lead the Berlin office.
was / were to + base form · was / were to have + participle
The new office was to open in June, but the permit was delayed.
signals: was going to / were going to
was about to / were about to

traps.bad: We are going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.
traps.good: We were going to launch in May, but the supplier was late.
why: Ein Plan aus der Vergangenheit braucht was oder were going to. Das Hilfsverb are gehört in die Gegenwart.
A plan from the past needs was or were going to. The auxiliary are belongs to the present.

traps.bad: I was about leaving when the client called.
traps.good: I was about to leave when the client called.
why: Das deutsche „gerade am Gehen“ führt zu „about leaving“. Englisch sagt about to und die Grundform.
The German “gerade am Gehen” leads to “about leaving”. English says about to and the base form.

traps.bad: In 2015 she joined the firm and will later lead the Berlin office.
traps.good: In 2015 she joined the firm and would later lead the Berlin office.
why: Wer aus der Vergangenheit auf Späteres blickt, braucht would. Will gehört in die Gegenwart.
If you look from the past at something later, you need would. Will belongs to the present.

traps.bad: The new office should open in June, but the permit was delayed.
traps.good: The new office was to open in June, but the permit was delayed.
why: Das deutsche „sollte“ wird hier nicht zu should. Für einen Plan in der Vergangenheit gilt was to.
The German “sollte” does not become should here. For a plan in the past was to is used.

core: Hardly, scarcely und barely sind schon verneint. None of und neither of stehen für „keiner“. No longer heißt „nicht mehr“. A number of nimmt Plural, the number of Singular.
Hardly, scarcely and barely are already negative. None of and neither of stand for “not one”. No longer means “not anymore”. A number of takes plural, the number of singular.
why: Im Beruf brauchst du genaue Mengen: „None of the suppliers …“, „We no longer offer …“, „The number of complaints has fallen“. Wann ja, wann nein: Im Gespräch sagt man oft „nobody“ und „not anymore“, in Berichten und Mails passen none of und no longer besser.

At work you need exact amounts: “None of the suppliers …”, “We no longer offer …”, “The number of complaints has fallen”. When yes, when no: in conversation people often say “nobody” and “not anymore”, in reports and emails none of and no longer fit better.
contrast: Nicht verwechseln: Das deutsche „nicht mehr“ ist bei der Zeit no longer, nicht no more. „Kaum“ braucht kein zweites not.
Do not mix up: the German “nicht mehr” is no longer for time, not no more. “Kaum” needs no second not.
steps: Keiner von diesen? none of / neither of.
Kaum? hardly / scarcely / barely, ohne not.
Nicht mehr? no longer.
Einige oder die Zahl? a number of / the number of.
Not one of these? none of / neither of.
Barely? hardly / scarcely / barely, without not.
Not anymore? no longer.
Several or the figure? a number of / the number of.
forms: none of / neither of (two) / not any of + the + noun
None of the suppliers has replied yet.
hardly / scarcely / barely + any / ever / enough (without not)
There was hardly any time left to prepare.
no longer + verb · not … any longer / anymore (at the end)
We no longer offer this service.
a number of, the number of
a number of, the number of
a number of + plural (plural verb) · the number of + plural (singular verb)
A number of customers have complained about the delay.
signals: a number of / the number of
a number of, the number of
a number of, the number of

traps.bad: No one of the suppliers has replied yet.
traps.good: None of the suppliers has replied yet.
why: Für „keiner von …“ mit Nomen sagt man none of. No one of ist deutsch gedacht.
For “not one of …” with a noun you say none of. No one of is German thinking.

traps.bad: We did not hardly have any time to prepare.
traps.good: We hardly had any time to prepare.
why: Hardly ist schon verneint. Das deutsche „kaum“ braucht im Englischen kein zweites not.
Hardly is already negative. The German “kaum” needs no second not in English.

traps.bad: We no more offer this service.
traps.good: We no longer offer this service.
why: Für „nicht mehr“ bei der Zeit sagt man no longer. No more steht bei Mengen und vor Nomen.
For “not anymore” in time you say no longer. No more is used with amounts and before nouns.

traps.bad: The number of customers have risen sharply this year.
traps.good: The number of customers has risen sharply this year.
why: Beim Kern „the number“ steht das Verb im Singular. Bei „a number of“ steht es im Plural.
With the core “the number” the verb is singular. With “a number of” it is plural.

tasks.prompt: Soften this for a client: Your price ___ a bit above our budget.
tasks.expl: „might be“ plus „a bit“ macht aus einem Vorwurf eine vorsichtige Einschätzung.
tasks.expl_en: “Might be” plus “a bit” turns a complaint into a careful assessment.

tasks.prompt: ___ worth considering a phased rollout.
tasks.expl: Feste Einleitung: It might be worth + -ing. „Maybe“ ersetzt kein Modalverb.
tasks.expl_en: Fixed lead-in: It might be worth + -ing. “Maybe” does not replace a modal verb.

tasks.prompt: Choose the softest way to disagree with a client: ___
options: I'm not sure that's quite right.
tasks.answer: I'm not sure that's quite right.
tasks.expl: „I'm not sure … quite …“ widerspricht, ohne das Gegenüber bloßzustellen.
tasks.expl_en: “I'm not sure … quite …” disagrees without putting the other person on the spot.

tasks.prompt: It ___ worth revisiting the timeline before we sign.
tasks.expl: Vorsichtiger Vorschlag: „might be worth“ + -ing-Form.
tasks.expl_en: A careful suggestion: might be worth + -ing.

tasks.prompt: I'd be inclined ___ with the finance team.
tasks.expl: Nach „be inclined“ folgt „to“ + Grundform: I’d be inclined to start with the finance team.
tasks.expl_en: After “be inclined” use “to” + base verb: I’d be inclined to start with the finance team.

tasks.prompt: It ___ that the budget is tighter than we expected.
tasks.expl: „It seems that …“ stellt die Aussage als Eindruck dar, nicht als Tatsache.
tasks.expl_en: “It seems that …” presents the statement as an impression, not a fact.

tasks.prompt: The migration could take ___ longer than planned.
tasks.expl: „slightly“ schwächt die schlechte Nachricht ab; „hugely“ würde sie verstärken.
tasks.expl_en: “Slightly” softens the bad news; “hugely” would make it stronger.

tasks.prompt: The rollout will fail without training. → Without training, the rollout ___ into difficulties.
tasks.expl: Statt einer sicheren Vorhersage (will fail) eine Möglichkeit mit might.
tasks.expl_en: Instead of a certain prediction (will fail), a possibility with might.

tasks.prompt: Start with a pilot. → I'd be inclined ___ with a pilot.
tasks.expl: Aus der Anweisung wird eine persönliche Neigung: I'd be inclined to + Grundform.
tasks.expl_en: The instruction becomes a personal preference: I'd be inclined to + base form.

tasks.prompt: Your team is not ready. → I'm not sure your team is ___ ready yet.
tasks.expl: „not quite“ macht aus einem harten Urteil eine milde Einschätzung.
tasks.expl_en: “Not quite” turns a hard judgment into a mild one.

tasks.prompt: It might be worth to check the retention periods first.
tasks.answer: It might be worth checking the retention periods first.
tasks.expl: Nach „worth“ steht die -ing-Form, nie to + Grundform.
tasks.expl_en: “Worth” is followed by the -ing form, never by to + base form.

tasks.prompt: I would be inclined starting with the invoices.
tasks.answer: I would be inclined to start with the invoices.
accepted: I'd be inclined to start with the invoices.
tasks.expl: Nach „be inclined“ folgt „to“ + Grundform.
tasks.expl_en: “Be inclined” needs to + base form.

tasks.prompt: It seems as the budget is tighter this year.
tasks.answer: It seems that the budget is tighter this year.
accepted: It seems the budget is tighter this year.
It seems as if the budget is tighter this year.
tasks.expl: Nach „It seems“ folgt „that“ (oder nichts), nicht „as“.
tasks.expl_en: “It seems” is followed by “that” (or nothing), not “as”.

tasks.prompt: I ___ whether you could share the requirements by Friday.
tasks.expl: Die Verlaufsform der Vergangenheit macht die Bitte höflich – gemeint ist jetzt.
tasks.expl_en: The past continuous makes the request polite – it still means now.

tasks.prompt: We ___ to sign before the end of Q3.
tasks.expl: „We were hoping …“ klingt weicher als „We want …“.
tasks.expl_en: “We were hoping …” sounds softer than “We want …”.

tasks.prompt: Would it be possible ___ the trial by two weeks?
tasks.expl: Nach „Would it be possible“ folgt „to“ + Grundform.
tasks.expl_en: “Would it be possible” + to + base form.

tasks.prompt: I was wondering if you ___ join the call on Monday.
tasks.expl: Nach „I was wondering“ bleibt der Abstand: could statt can.
tasks.expl_en: After “I was wondering” the distance continues: could instead of can.

tasks.prompt: Which request sounds most diplomatic to a new client? ___
options: Send me the data by Friday.
I was wondering whether you could send the data by Friday.
You must send the data by Friday.
I want the data by Friday.
tasks.answer: I was wondering whether you could send the data by Friday.
tasks.expl: Vergangenheit plus could: eine Bitte, die man ablehnen darf.
tasks.expl_en: Past tense plus could: a request the client can decline.

tasks.prompt: That timeline could be a bit ___ for us.
tasks.expl: Untertreibung: „tricky“ heißt höflich „kaum machbar“.
tasks.expl_en: Understatement: “tricky” is a polite way of saying “hardly possible”.

tasks.prompt: We ___ to get your feedback this week.
tasks.expl: „were hoping“ ist die höfliche, distanzierte Form des Wunsches.
tasks.expl_en: “Were hoping” is the polite, distanced way to express a wish.

tasks.prompt: Can you move the demo to Thursday? → I was wondering whether you ___ the demo to Thursday.
tasks.expl: Aus der direkten Frage wird eine indirekte Bitte mit could.
tasks.expl_en: The direct question becomes an indirect request with could.

tasks.prompt: Your offer is too expensive. → Your offer ___ be a bit of a stretch for our budget.
tasks.expl: Einwand mit Abstand: „could be a bit of a stretch“ statt „is too expensive“.
tasks.expl_en: An objection with distance: could be a bit of a stretch instead of is too expensive.

tasks.prompt: We want a discount. → We ___ hoping for a small discount.
tasks.expl: „We were hoping for …“ macht aus der Forderung einen Wunsch.
tasks.expl_en: “We were hoping for …” turns the demand into a wish.

tasks.prompt: We were hoping you can confirm the date.
tasks.answer: We were hoping you could confirm the date.
accepted: We were hoping that you could confirm the date.
We were hoping you would confirm the date.
We were hoping that you would confirm the date.
We were hoping you'd confirm the date.
We are hoping you can confirm the date.
tasks.expl: Nach der Distanz-Vergangenheit steht could, nicht can.
tasks.expl_en: After the distancing past, use could, not can.

tasks.prompt: I was wondering whether could you share the price list.
tasks.answer: I was wondering whether you could share the price list.
accepted: I was wondering if you could share the price list.
I was wondering whether you would share the price list.
I was wondering if you would share the price list.
tasks.expl: Indirekte Frage: normale Wortstellung, Subjekt vor Verb.
tasks.expl_en: Indirect question: normal word order, subject before verb.

tasks.prompt: I was wondering if you can send the signed contract today.
tasks.answer: I was wondering if you could send the signed contract today.
accepted: I was wondering whether you could send the signed contract today.
I was wondering if you would send the signed contract today.
I was wondering whether you would send the signed contract today.
I am wondering if you can send the signed contract today.
I'm wondering if you can send the signed contract today.
tasks.expl: „I was wondering if …“ verlangt could statt can.
tasks.expl_en: “I was wondering if …” needs could instead of can.

tasks.prompt: What we really need ___ a clear timeline.
tasks.expl: Ein What-Satz zählt als eine einzige Sache, deshalb steht „is“: What we really need is a clear timeline.
tasks.expl_en: A what-clause counts as one single thing, so use “is”: What we really need is a clear timeline.

tasks.prompt: Not only ___ we reduce storage costs, but we also improved compliance.
tasks.expl: Inversion nach „Not only“: Hilfsverb vor das Subjekt; Vergangenheit → did.
tasks.expl_en: Inversion after “Not only”: auxiliary before the subject; past → did.

tasks.prompt: It was the CFO ___ approved the budget in the end.
tasks.expl: It-Cleft mit Person: who (oder that).
tasks.expl_en: It-cleft with a person: who (or that).

tasks.prompt: Rarely ___ we seen such a fast rollout.
tasks.expl: Nach „Rarely“ am Satzanfang: Hilfsverb vor das Subjekt – have we seen.
tasks.expl_en: After “Rarely” at the start: auxiliary before the subject – have we seen.

tasks.prompt: ___ convinced them was the audit trail.
tasks.expl: What-Cleft: „What convinced them was …“ betont den Grund.
tasks.expl_en: What-cleft: “What convinced them was …” stresses the reason.

tasks.prompt: Never ___ a customer migrate 20 million documents in one weekend.
tasks.expl: Nach „Never“ am Satzanfang wird umgestellt: Das Hilfsverb steht vor dem Subjekt – „Never have I seen …“.
tasks.expl_en: After “Never” at the start of a sentence the order changes: the auxiliary goes before the subject – “Never have I seen …”.

tasks.prompt: Only after the pilot ___ the full rollout.
tasks.expl: „Only after …“ am Satzanfang löst Inversion aus: did they approve.
tasks.expl_en: “Only after …” at the start triggers inversion: did they approve.

tasks.prompt: We really need better search. → What we really need ___ better search.
tasks.expl: What-Cleft: „What“ + Subjekt + Verb + „is“ + das Betonte.
tasks.expl_en: What-cleft: What + subject + verb + is + focus.

tasks.prompt: The audit trail convinced them. → It was the audit trail ___ convinced them.
tasks.expl: It-Cleft mit einer Sache: that.
tasks.expl_en: It-cleft with a thing: that.

tasks.prompt: We cut costs and we also improved compliance. → Not only ___ costs, but we also improved compliance.
tasks.expl: Nach „Not only“ am Satzanfang steht „did“ + Subjekt + Grundform: Not only did we cut costs, …
tasks.expl_en: After “Not only” at the start use “did” + subject + base verb: Not only did we cut costs, …

tasks.prompt: What we need are a partner who understands compliance.
tasks.answer: What we need is a partner who understands compliance.
tasks.expl: Nach einem What-Satz steht in der Regel „is“: What we need is a partner …
tasks.expl_en: After a what-clause the verb is usually “is”: What we need is a partner …

tasks.prompt: Rarely we have seen such a fast approval.
tasks.answer: Rarely have we seen such a fast approval.
tasks.expl: Nach „Rarely“ am Satzanfang: Hilfsverb vor das Subjekt.
tasks.expl_en: After “Rarely” at the start: auxiliary before the subject.

tasks.prompt: Not only it saves time, but it also reduces errors.
tasks.answer: Not only does it save time, but it also reduces errors.
tasks.expl: Nach „Not only“ am Satzanfang steht „does“ + Subjekt + Grundform: Not only does it save time, …
tasks.expl_en: After “Not only” at the start use “does” + subject + base verb: Not only does it save time, …

tasks.prompt: The pilot went well. ___, the timeline for the rollout is still tight.
tasks.expl: „That said“ schränkt das Positive ein – wie „Allerdings“.
tasks.expl_en: “That said” qualifies the good news – like “however”.

tasks.prompt: Anna mentioned the audit trail. ___, we could also show the retention rules.
tasks.expl: Anknüpfen an den Beitrag einer anderen Person: To build on that.
tasks.expl_en: Building on someone else's point: To build on that.

tasks.prompt: ___, the pilot saved the team about ten hours a week.
tasks.expl: Mit „In short“ kündigst du das Fazit an: kurz gesagt.
tasks.expl_en: Use “In short” to introduce the conclusion.

tasks.prompt: The price is higher than the old system. ___, you save on hardware and maintenance.
tasks.expl: Gegensatz zwischen zwei Seiten: „On the other hand“.
tasks.expl_en: A contrast between two sides: On the other hand.

tasks.prompt: Coming back ___ your question about pricing, the licenses are per user.
tasks.expl: Feste Verbindung: „coming back to“.
tasks.expl_en: Fixed phrase: coming back to.

tasks.prompt: To build ___ what Mark said, we could start with the invoices.
tasks.expl: Feste Verbindung: „build on something“.
tasks.expl_en: Fixed phrase: build on something.

tasks.prompt: Having ___ that, we still need IT to sign off.
tasks.expl: „Having said that“ ist eine feste Wendung zum Einschränken.
tasks.expl_en: “Having said that” is a fixed phrase for qualifying.

tasks.prompt: All ___ all, the migration went smoothly.
tasks.expl: Feste Wendung zum Zusammenfassen: All in all.
tasks.expl_en: Fixed phrase for summing up: All in all.

tasks.prompt: The demo was good. But we still need a business case. → The demo was good. That ___, we still need a business case.
tasks.expl: „That said“ ersetzt das schlichte „But“ und klingt strukturierter.
tasks.expl_en: “That said” replaces a plain “But” and sounds more structured.

tasks.prompt: I want to return to the topic of security. → Coming ___ security, all data is encrypted at rest.
tasks.expl: Zurück zu einem früheren Punkt: Coming back to + Thema.
tasks.expl_en: Back to an earlier point: Coming back to + topic.

tasks.prompt: On the other side, the cloud version needs no local servers.
tasks.answer: On the other hand, the cloud version needs no local servers.
tasks.expl: Gegensatz heißt „on the other hand“, „side“ ist ein Ort.
tasks.expl_en: The contrast is “on the other hand”; “side” is a place.

tasks.prompt: To build up on that, we could add a second department.
tasks.answer: To build on that, we could add a second department.
accepted: To build upon that, we could add a second department.
tasks.expl: Es heißt „build on“ (oder „build upon“), nicht „build up on“.
tasks.expl_en: It is “build on” (or “build upon”), not “build up on”.

tasks.prompt: The ___ of the new archive will start in May.
tasks.expl: Hier brauchst du ein Nomen. Zu „implement“ gehört „implementation“.
tasks.expl_en: You need a noun here. The noun for “implement” is “implementation”.

tasks.prompt: After the ___ of the budget, we will order the licenses.
tasks.expl: Hier brauchst du ein Nomen. Zu „approve“ gehört „approval“.
tasks.expl_en: You need a noun here. The noun for “approve” is “approval”.

tasks.prompt: We expect a significant ___ in storage costs.
tasks.expl: Nomen zu reduce: reduction – mit „in“ für den Bereich.
tasks.expl_en: Noun of reduce: reduction – with “in” for the area.

tasks.prompt: Please confirm the ___ date for the scanners.
tasks.expl: Hier brauchst du ein Nomen. Zu „deliver“ gehört „delivery“.
tasks.expl_en: You need a noun here. The noun for “deliver” is “delivery”.

tasks.prompt: The ___ to move to the cloud was made in March.
tasks.expl: Hier brauchst du ein Nomen. Zu „decide“ gehört „decision“.
tasks.expl_en: You need a noun here. The noun for “decide” is “decision”.

tasks.prompt: Upon ___ of the contract, we will send you the access data.
tasks.expl: Nomen zu receive: receipt – „upon receipt of“ ist eine feste Mail-Wendung.
tasks.expl_en: Noun of receive: receipt – “upon receipt of” is a fixed email phrase.

tasks.prompt: The ___ of the legacy data took two weeks.
tasks.expl: Nach „The … of“ steht ein Nomen, kein Verb: the migration of the legacy data.
tasks.expl_en: After “The … of” use a noun, not a verb: the migration of the legacy data.

tasks.prompt: We will migrate the data in June. → The ___ of the data is planned for June.
tasks.expl: Aus dem Verb migrate wird das Nomen migration.
tasks.expl_en: The verb migrate becomes the noun migration.

tasks.prompt: After the board approves it, we can start. → After the board's ___, we can start.
tasks.expl: Aus dem Nebensatz wird ein Nomen: the board's approval.
tasks.expl_en: The clause becomes a noun: the board's approval.

tasks.prompt: We need to decide by Friday. → We need a ___ by Friday.
tasks.expl: Das Nomen zu „decide“ ist „decision“: We need a decision by Friday.
tasks.expl_en: The noun for “decide” is “decision”: We need a decision by Friday.

tasks.prompt: The implement of the new workflow starts next week.
tasks.answer: The implementation of the new workflow starts next week.
tasks.expl: Nach „The“ steht das Nomen implementation, nicht das Verb.
tasks.expl_en: After “The”, use the noun implementation, not the verb.

tasks.prompt: We look forward to the approve of the pilot.
tasks.answer: We look forward to the approval of the pilot.
tasks.expl: Hier brauchst du ein Nomen. Zu „approve“ gehört „approval“.
tasks.expl_en: You need a noun here. The noun for “approve” is “approval”.

tasks.prompt: ___ the contract, our legal team approved it.
tasks.expl: Erst geprüft, dann freigegeben: Having + 3. Form.
tasks.expl_en: First reviewed, then approved: Having + past participle.

tasks.prompt: ___ OCR, the system reads every incoming invoice.
tasks.expl: Wenn etwas das Mittel ist oder gleichzeitig passiert, nimmst du die -ing-Form: Using OCR, the system reads every invoice.
tasks.expl_en: When something is the means or happens at the same time, use the -ing form: Using OCR, the system reads every invoice.

tasks.prompt: ___ in German data centers, the documents stay GDPR-compliant.
tasks.expl: Passive Bedeutung (die Dokumente werden gespeichert): 3. Form.
tasks.expl_en: Passive meaning (the documents are stored): past participle.

tasks.prompt: Having ___ the pilot, we moved on to the rollout.
tasks.expl: Nach „Having“ folgt die 3. Verbform: Having finished the pilot, we moved on.
tasks.expl_en: After “Having” use the past participle: Having finished the pilot, we moved on.

tasks.prompt: ___ the demo, the IT lead asked about single sign-on.
tasks.expl: Erst die Demo gesehen, dann gefragt: Having + 3. Form.
tasks.expl_en: First saw the demo, then asked: Having + past participle.

tasks.prompt: ___ by the auditors, the new process is now standard.
tasks.expl: Der Prozess wurde geprüft. Das ist passiv, deshalb steht nur die 3. Verbform: Approved by the auditors, …
tasks.expl_en: The process was approved. That is passive, so use only the past participle: Approved by the auditors, …

tasks.prompt: ___ in the cloud, the archive needs no local servers.
tasks.expl: Der Zustand läuft gleichzeitig, deshalb nimmst du die -ing-Form: Running in the cloud, the archive needs no local servers.
tasks.expl_en: The state happens at the same time, so use the -ing form: Running in the cloud, the archive needs no local servers.

tasks.prompt: After we had tested the workflow, we trained the users. → ___ the workflow, we trained the users.
tasks.expl: Vorzeitig und gleiches Subjekt: Having + 3. Form.
tasks.expl_en: Completed before, same subject: Having + past participle.

tasks.prompt: Because it runs in the cloud, the archive scales automatically. → ___ in the cloud, the archive scales automatically.
tasks.expl: Grund und gleichzeitig: -ing-Form statt „Because it runs“.
tasks.expl_en: Reason and at the same time: -ing form instead of “Because it runs”.

tasks.prompt: The report was written in May, and it is already out of date. → ___ in May, the report is already out of date.
tasks.expl: Der Bericht wurde geschrieben, er schreibt nicht selbst. Das ist passiv, deshalb steht nur die 3. Verbform: Written in May, …
tasks.expl_en: The report was written; it does not write anything itself. That is passive, so use only the past participle: Written in May, …

tasks.prompt: Having sign the contract, the customer received the access data.
tasks.answer: Having signed the contract, the customer received the access data.
tasks.expl: Nach „Having“ folgt die 3. Verbform, hier „signed“: Having signed the contract, …
tasks.expl_en: After “Having” use the past participle, here “signed”: Having signed the contract, …

tasks.prompt: Having receiving your feedback, we updated the offer.
tasks.answer: Having received your feedback, we updated the offer.
tasks.expl: Nach „Having“ folgt die 3. Verbform („received“), nicht -ing: Having received your feedback, …
tasks.expl_en: After “Having” use the past participle (“received”), not -ing: Having received your feedback, …

tasks.prompt: Use the new search, you can find any invoice in seconds.
tasks.answer: Using the new search, you can find any invoice in seconds.
tasks.expl: Am Satzanfang nimmst du für das Mittel die -ing-Form: Using the new search, you can find any invoice.
tasks.expl_en: At the start of the sentence use the -ing form for the means: Using the new search, you can find any invoice.

tasks.prompt: We need your decision ___ the end of Q3.
tasks.expl: Für eine Frist („spätestens bis“) nimmst du „by“: by the end of Q3.
tasks.expl_en: For a deadline (“no later than”) use “by”: by the end of Q3.

tasks.prompt: The trial runs ___ June 30, then it ends automatically.
tasks.expl: Für eine Dauer „bis zu“ einem Zeitpunkt nimmst du „until“: The trial runs until June 30.
tasks.expl_en: For a duration “up to” a point in time use “until”: The trial runs until June 30.

tasks.prompt: We can set up the test system ___ two weeks.
tasks.expl: Für „innerhalb“ eines Zeitraums nimmst du „within“: within two weeks.
tasks.expl_en: For “inside” a period of time use “within”: within two weeks.

tasks.prompt: ___ June 1, all invoices must be archived electronically.
tasks.expl: Für „ab“ einem Stichtag nimmst du „As of“: As of June 1, …
tasks.expl_en: For “from” a key date onward use “As of”: As of June 1, …

tasks.prompt: The cloud version costs ___ of the on-premise license.
tasks.expl: „a fraction of“ = nur ein kleiner Teil davon.
tasks.expl_en: “A fraction of” = only a small part of it.

tasks.prompt: We process ___ 40,000 invoices a month – the exact number is 39,600.
tasks.expl: Knapp unter einer Zahl: just under.
tasks.expl_en: Slightly below a number: just under.

tasks.prompt: Our new client has ___ many users as the old one – 2,000 instead of 1,000.
tasks.expl: Doppelt so viele: „twice as many as“.
tasks.expl_en: Double the number: twice as many as.

tasks.prompt: Please send the signed offer ___ Friday at the latest.
tasks.expl: „at the latest“ zeigt eine Frist: by.
tasks.expl_en: “At the latest” signals a deadline: by.

tasks.prompt: About 60% of the documents are scanned. → ___ 60% of the documents are scanned.
tasks.expl: „Roughly“ ist im Geschäftsenglisch üblicher als „about“ und kündigt eine gerundete Zahl an.
tasks.expl_en: “Roughly” is more common than “about” in business English and signals a rounded figure.

tasks.prompt: The rollout must be finished before September 30 at the latest. → The rollout must be finished ___ September 30.
tasks.expl: Frist: „by September 30“.
tasks.expl_en: Deadline: by September 30.

tasks.prompt: We will send you the offer until Wednesday.
tasks.answer: We will send you the offer by Wednesday.
accepted: We will send you the offer no later than Wednesday.
We will send you the offer on or before Wednesday.
tasks.expl: Frist heißt „by“, nicht „until“.
tasks.expl_en: A deadline is “by”, not “until”.

tasks.prompt: The new system is two times faster as the old one.
tasks.answer: The new system is twice as fast as the old one.
accepted: The new system is twice as fast as the old system.
The new system is two times as fast as the old one.
The new system is two times as fast as the old system.
tasks.expl: Vergleich: „twice as“ + Adjektiv + „as“.
tasks.expl_en: Comparison: twice as + adjective + as.

tasks.prompt: Please call me as soon as the shipment ___ at the warehouse.
tasks.expl: Nach „as soon as“ steht bei Zukünftigem das Präsens, nicht „will“.
tasks.expl_en: After “as soon as”, future meaning takes the present simple, not will.

tasks.prompt: We won't sign the contract until the legal team ___ the final draft.
tasks.expl: Nach „until“ steht das Präsens; „will“ gehört nur in den Hauptsatz.
tasks.expl_en: After “until” use the present; will belongs only in the main clause.

tasks.prompt: By the time you read this email, I ___ the presentation.
tasks.expl: „By the time“ meint einen Zeitpunkt, bis zu dem etwas abgeschlossen ist: will have + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: “By the time” points to a moment by which something is complete: will have + participle.

tasks.prompt: I'll text you when I ___ home tonight.
tasks.expl: Nach „when“ steht das Präsens, auch bei Zukunftsbezug.
tasks.expl_en: After “when” the present is used, even for future meaning.

tasks.prompt: Let's start the meeting as soon as everyone ___ here.
tasks.expl: Im Zeitsatz steht Present Perfect oder Präsens, nicht „will have“.
tasks.expl_en: In the time clause use present perfect or present simple, not will have.

tasks.prompt: I'll send you the report after I ___ the numbers.
tasks.expl: Nach „after“ bei Zukünftigem: Present Perfect (oder Präsens).
tasks.expl_en: After “after” with future meaning: present perfect (or present simple).

tasks.prompt: Don't switch off the server until the backup ___ completed.
tasks.expl: Nach „until“ steht das Präsens oder Present Perfect: „has been completed“.
tasks.expl_en: After “until” use present simple or present perfect: “has been completed”.

tasks.prompt: The call will end soon. Then I'll email you. → I'll email you as soon as the call ___.
tasks.expl: Der Zeitsatz mit „as soon as“ steht im Präsens.
tasks.expl_en: The “as soon as” clause stays in the present.

tasks.prompt: We will wait for the approval. Then we will start. → We won't start until the approval ___.
tasks.expl: Nach „until“ steht das Präsens oder Present Perfect.
tasks.expl_en: After “until” use the present simple or present perfect.

tasks.prompt: I will call you when I will arrive at the airport.
tasks.answer: I will call you when I arrive at the airport.
accepted: I'll call you when I arrive at the airport.
I will call you when I get to the airport.
I'll call you when I get to the airport.
I will call you when I have arrived at the airport.
I'll call you when I have arrived at the airport.
I will call you when I reach the airport.
I'll call you when I reach the airport.
tasks.expl: Nach „when“ steht das Präsens, nicht „will“.
tasks.expl_en: After “when” the present is needed, not will.

tasks.prompt: We'll go home as soon as the meeting will be over.
tasks.answer: We'll go home as soon as the meeting is over.
accepted: We will go home as soon as the meeting is over.
tasks.expl: Nach „as soon as“ ist „will“ falsch, es steht das Präsens.
tasks.expl_en: After “as soon as”, will is wrong; use the present.

tasks.prompt: Please wait here until the manager will come back.
tasks.answer: Please wait here until the manager comes back.
accepted: Please wait here until the manager has come back.
Please wait here until the manager gets back.
Please wait here until the manager returns.
Please wait here until the manager has returned.
Please wait here until the manager is back.
tasks.expl: Nach „until“ steht das Präsens statt „will come“.
tasks.expl_en: After “until” use the present instead of will come.

tasks.prompt: We'll miss the deadline ___ we hire extra staff.
tasks.expl: „Unless“ = „wenn nicht“: ohne zusätzliches Personal verpassen wir die Frist.
tasks.expl_en: “Unless” = “if not”: without extra staff we'll miss the deadline.

tasks.prompt: You can use the company car ___ you return it by Friday.
tasks.expl: „As long as“ nennt die Bedingung, unter der etwas erlaubt ist.
tasks.expl_en: “As long as” states the condition under which something is allowed.

tasks.prompt: Send me the invoice today. ___, we can't process the payment this month.
tasks.expl: „Otherwise“ steht im neuen Satz und nennt die Folge, wenn die Bedingung fehlt.
tasks.expl_en: “Otherwise” starts a new sentence and names the result if the condition isn't met.

tasks.prompt: ___ your support, the project would never have launched on time.
tasks.expl: „But for“ + Nomen heißt „ohne“ und passt zu would have + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: “But for” + noun means “without” and fits would have + participle.

tasks.prompt: The client will renew ___ that we improve our support.
tasks.expl: „Provided that“ nennt die Bedingung; „providing“ ist ebenfalls möglich.
tasks.expl_en: “Provided that” names the condition; “providing” is also possible.

tasks.prompt: We'll cancel the event ___ enough people sign up by Monday.
tasks.expl: „Unless“ = wir sagen ab, wenn sich nicht genug Leute anmelden.
tasks.expl_en: “Unless” = we'll cancel if not enough people sign up.

tasks.prompt: You may work remotely as ___ as you stay reachable.
tasks.expl: „As long as“ heißt „solange / sofern“.
tasks.expl_en: “As long as” means “provided that”.

tasks.prompt: If we don't get the budget, we can't hire anyone. → We can't hire anyone ___ we get the budget.
tasks.expl: „Unless“ ersetzt „if … not“.
tasks.expl_en: “Unless” replaces “if … not”.

tasks.prompt: Without your help, we would have failed. → ___ your help, we would have failed.
accepted: If it had not been for
tasks.expl: „But for“ + Nomen = „ohne“ im Rückblick.
tasks.expl_en: “But for” + noun = “without” in hindsight.

tasks.prompt: Unless you don't sign today, the offer expires.
tasks.answer: Unless you sign today, the offer expires.
accepted: Unless you sign today the offer expires.
tasks.expl: „Unless“ enthält die Verneinung schon; kein zweites „don't“.
tasks.expl_en: “Unless” already carries the negation; no second “don't”.

tasks.prompt: I'll attend the workshop as long as it will not overlap with my client call.
tasks.answer: I'll attend the workshop as long as it doesn't overlap with my client call.
accepted: I'll attend the workshop as long as it does not overlap with my client call.
tasks.expl: Nach „as long as“ steht das Präsens, nicht „will“.
tasks.expl_en: After “as long as” use the present, not will.

tasks.prompt: You can borrow my laptop provided you will return it tomorrow.
tasks.answer: You can borrow my laptop provided you return it tomorrow.
accepted: You can borrow my laptop provided that you return it tomorrow.
tasks.expl: Nach „provided“ steht das Präsens.
tasks.expl_en: After “provided” the present is used.

tasks.prompt: The new software ___ by the end of the month.
tasks.expl: Modalverb + be + Partizip bildet das Passiv.
tasks.expl_en: Modal + be + participle forms the passive.

tasks.prompt: The office ___ by the time we arrived.
tasks.expl: Vorzeitigkeit im Passiv: had been + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: Earlier past in the passive: had been + participle.

tasks.prompt: The CEO ___ to be planning a merger.
tasks.expl: „Is said to“ gibt ein Gerücht sachlich wieder.
tasks.expl_en: “Is said to” reports a rumor in a neutral way.

tasks.prompt: I don't like ___ by customers while I'm in meetings.
tasks.expl: Nach „like“ steht das Passiv als Gerundium: being + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: After “like” the passive appears as a gerund: being + participle.

tasks.prompt: The contract has to ___ before Friday.
tasks.expl: Modal oder „has to“ + be + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: Modal or “has to” + be + participle.

tasks.prompt: The company is ___ to have lost millions last year.
tasks.expl: Persönliches Passiv: is said / reported / believed to have + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: Personal passive: is said / reported / believed to have + participle.

tasks.prompt: I hate ___ interrupted when I'm presenting.
tasks.expl: Nach „hate“ steht „being“ + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: After “hate” use “being” + participle.

tasks.prompt: People say that the new manager is very strict. → The new manager ___ to be very strict.
tasks.expl: „People say that …“ wird zu „X is said to …“.
tasks.expl_en: “People say that …” becomes “X is said to …”.

tasks.prompt: Someone must repair the printer today. → The printer ___ today.
tasks.expl: Modal + be + Partizip.
tasks.expl_en: Modal + be + participle.

tasks.prompt: The documents must be send to the client by noon.
tasks.answer: The documents must be sent to the client by noon.
tasks.expl: Nach „be“ steht das Partizip „sent“.
tasks.expl_en: After “be” the participle “sent” is required.

tasks.prompt: The plant is believed closing next year.
tasks.answer: The plant is believed to be closing next year.
tasks.expl: Persönliches Passiv: believed + to-Infinitiv.
tasks.expl_en: Personal passive: believed + to-infinitive.
accepted: The plant is believed to close next year.

tasks.prompt: Our offer has been accepted by the client yesterday.
tasks.answer: Our offer was accepted by the client yesterday.
accepted: Our offer was accepted yesterday by the client.
tasks.expl: Mit „yesterday“ steht das Simple Past, nicht das Present Perfect.
tasks.expl_en: With “yesterday” use the simple past, not the present perfect.

tasks.prompt: She admitted ___ the wrong figures to the board.
tasks.expl: Nach „admit“ steht die -ing-Form.
tasks.expl_en: After “admit” the -ing form follows.

tasks.prompt: My lawyer advised me ___ the document yet.
tasks.expl: „Advise“ + Person + to-Infinitiv; die Verneinung steht vor „to“.
tasks.expl_en: “Advise” + person + to-infinitive; the negation goes before “to”.

tasks.prompt: He insisted ___ for the dinner.
tasks.expl: „Insist“ verlangt die Präposition „on“ + -ing.
tasks.expl_en: “Insist” takes the preposition “on” + -ing.

tasks.prompt: The consultant recommended ___ the pilot in March.
tasks.expl: „Recommend“ steht mit -ing oder that-Satz; Person + to ist im US-Englisch unüblich.
tasks.expl_en: “Recommend” takes -ing or a that-clause; person + to is uncommon in US English.

tasks.prompt: She suggested ___ the deadline to Thursday.
tasks.expl: Nach „suggest“ steht -ing.
tasks.expl_en: After “suggest” use -ing.

tasks.prompt: The doctor advised him ___ more rest.
tasks.expl: „Advise“ + Person + to-Infinitiv.
tasks.expl_en: “Advise” + person + to-infinitive.

tasks.prompt: The manager denied ___ the error.
tasks.expl: Nach „deny“ steht -ing.
tasks.expl_en: After “deny” use -ing.

tasks.prompt: 'I'll cover the costs,' he said. → He offered ___ the costs.
tasks.expl: „Offer“ + to-Infinitiv.
tasks.expl_en: “Offer” + to-infinitive.

tasks.prompt: 'Don't discuss the deal with anyone,' she told me. → She warned me ___ the deal with anyone.
tasks.expl: „Warn“ + Person + not to + Verb.
tasks.expl_en: “Warn” + person + not to + verb.

tasks.prompt: He suggested me to take a different route.
tasks.answer: He suggested that I take a different route.
accepted: He suggested that I should take a different route.
He suggested I take a different route.

tasks.expl_en: After “not only” comes “did” plus the base form.

tasks.prompt: Rarely we get such positive feedback from clients.
tasks.answer: Rarely do we get such positive feedback from clients.
tasks.expl: Inversion nach „rarely“.
tasks.expl_en: Inversion after “rarely”.

tasks.prompt: He explained clearly the plan to the team.
tasks.answer: He explained the plan clearly to the team.
accepted: He clearly explained the plan to the team.
He explained the plan to the team clearly.
tasks.expl: Zwischen Verb und Objekt steht kein Adverb.
tasks.expl_en: No adverb goes between verb and object.

tasks.prompt: No sooner we had signed the contract than the prices rose.
tasks.answer: No sooner had we signed the contract than the prices rose.
tasks.expl: Inversion nach „no sooner“.
tasks.expl_en: Inversion after “no sooner”.

tasks.prompt: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
tasks.expl: Vor einem Nomen („the heavy traffic“) steht „despite“.
tasks.expl_en: Before a noun (“the heavy traffic”) comes “despite”.

tasks.prompt: The sales team hit its target, ___ the support team missed theirs.
tasks.expl: „whereas“ verbindet zwei gegensätzliche Aussagen.
tasks.expl_en: “Whereas” links two contrasting statements.

tasks.prompt: The server crashed twice last week; ___, we are moving to a new provider.
tasks.expl: „therefore“ zeigt die Folge; davor Semikolon, danach Komma.
tasks.expl_en: “Therefore” shows the result; semicolon before, comma after.

tasks.prompt: ___ the offer was generous, he turned it down.
tasks.expl: Vor einem ganzen Satz steht „although“.
tasks.expl_en: A full clause takes “although”.

tasks.prompt: She got the job ___ her lack of experience.
tasks.expl: Vor einem Nomen steht „despite“ oder „in spite of“.
tasks.expl_en: Before a noun comes “despite” or “in spite of”.

tasks.prompt: The prototype looks great; ___, it still needs a lot of testing.
tasks.expl: „however“ steht nach Semikolon und bekommt ein Komma.
tasks.expl_en: “However” follows a semicolon and takes a comma.

tasks.prompt: Prices are rising, ___ wages are staying flat.
tasks.expl: „while“ oder „whereas“ stellt zwei Dinge gegenüber.
tasks.expl_en: “While” or “whereas” contrasts two things.

tasks.prompt: It was raining, but we held the outdoor event. → We held the outdoor event in ___ of the rain.
tasks.expl: „in spite of“ steht vor einem Nomen.
tasks.expl_en: “In spite of” goes before a noun.

tasks.prompt: He was tired. He finished the presentation. → ___ he was tired, he finished the presentation.
tasks.expl: „although“ leitet einen Nebensatz des Gegensatzes ein.
tasks.expl_en: “Although” introduces a clause of contrast.

tasks.prompt: Despite we were short on time, we completed the audit.
tasks.answer: Although we were short on time, we completed the audit.
accepted: Despite being short on time, we completed the audit.
Despite the lack of time, we completed the audit.
Even though we were short on time, we completed the audit.
Though we were short on time, we completed the audit.
Despite the fact that we were short on time, we completed the audit.
In spite of being short on time, we completed the audit.
In spite of the lack of time, we completed the audit.
tasks.expl: Vor einem Satz steht „although“; „despite“ braucht Nomen oder -ing.
tasks.expl_en: A clause takes “although”; “despite” needs a noun or -ing.

tasks.prompt: In spite the delay, the project was a success.
tasks.answer: In spite of the delay, the project was a success.
accepted: Despite the delay, the project was a success.
tasks.expl: „in spite“ braucht „of“.
tasks.expl_en: “In spite” needs “of”.

tasks.prompt: The budget was approved, however the project is still on hold.
tasks.answer: The budget was approved; however, the project is still on hold.
accepted: The budget was approved. However, the project is still on hold.
The budget was approved, but the project is still on hold.
The budget was approved; nevertheless, the project is still on hold.
The budget was approved. Nevertheless, the project is still on hold.
The budget was approved; nonetheless, the project is still on hold.
Although the budget was approved, the project is still on hold.
tasks.expl: „however“ verbindet keine Sätze mit bloßem Komma.
tasks.expl_en: “However” cannot join clauses with just a comma.

tasks.prompt: The ___ we prepare, the more confident we feel.
tasks.expl: „the more …, the more …“ drückt eine parallele Entwicklung aus.
tasks.expl_en: “The more …, the more …” expresses a parallel development.

tasks.prompt: This year's results are ___ better than last year's.
tasks.expl: Vor einem Komparativ steht „far“ oder „much“, nicht „very“.
tasks.expl_en: Before a comparative, use “far” or “much”, not “very”.

tasks.prompt: The new tool isn't as complicated ___ the old one.
tasks.expl: „as … as“ ist die feste Gleichheitsform.
tasks.expl_en: “As … as” is the fixed equality form.

tasks.prompt: Our office is ___ than theirs.
tasks.expl: Kurze Adjektive bilden den Komparativ mit „-er“.
tasks.expl_en: Short adjectives form the comparative with “-er”.

tasks.prompt: The ___ the deadline, the more stressed the team gets.
tasks.expl: „the + Komparativ“ steht vor beiden Satzteilen.
tasks.expl_en: “The + comparative” stands before both clauses.

tasks.prompt: Our competitor's prices are far ___ than ours, so we win customers.
tasks.expl: Nach „far“ folgt ein Komparativ mit „than“.
tasks.expl_en: After “far” comes a comparative with “than”.

tasks.prompt: This quarter's profit is twice ___ high as last quarter's.
tasks.expl: Vielfache bilden „twice as … as“.
tasks.expl_en: Multiples use “twice as … as”.

tasks.prompt: The train is faster than the bus. → The bus is not ___ fast as the train.
tasks.expl: „not as … as“ drückt den Unterschied umgekehrt aus.
tasks.expl_en: “Not as … as” expresses the difference the other way around.

tasks.prompt: If we work more, we finish earlier. → The more we work, the ___ we finish.
tasks.expl: Nach „the more …“ folgt „the“ plus Komparativ.
tasks.expl_en: After “the more …” comes “the” plus a comparative.

tasks.prompt: This solution is more cheaper than the previous one.
tasks.answer: This solution is cheaper than the previous one.
tasks.expl: Kein „more“ vor einem „-er“-Komparativ.
tasks.expl_en: No “more” before an “-er” comparative.

tasks.prompt: Our sales are higher as last year.
tasks.answer: Our sales are higher than last year.
accepted: Our sales are higher than last year's.
tasks.expl: Nach dem Komparativ steht „than“.
tasks.expl_en: After the comparative comes “than”.

tasks.prompt: More we practice, better we get.
tasks.answer: The more we practice, the better we get.
tasks.expl: „the more …, the better …“ braucht zweimal „the“.
tasks.expl_en: “The more …, the better …” needs “the” twice.
